hook: Capable, but no plan yet? Start with one goal of their own and the steps to reach it.
intro: PATH 101 is a half-hour workshop on Tuesday mornings. Each person names something they want, in their own words, then works out the action steps and skills it will take to get there. Benny Carson Sr. runs it for students from middle school through college, and for adults who want a plan too.

bullets.text: The four parts of PATH, the frame Benny teaches around, for school and for life after it.

bullets.lead: Half an hour, Tuesdays at 7 a.m.

bullets.text: Some parents come along and work on a goal of their own.

heroImage.alt: A teenage girl sits at a desk writing in a notebook

why.title: When every answer is "I don't know."
paragraphs: "He has potential. He just doesn't apply himself." "She doesn't know what she wants." "I'm just figuring it out." Parents hear the first two at the kitchen table. Young adults say the last one about themselves. Many young people have never had anyone sit down with them, help them decide what they want and break it into steps.
That's where PATH 101 starts: with a goal that belongs to them, and a next step they chose.

options.title: Who PATH 101 is for

items.label: Middle and high school
items.title: Smart, likable, no plan yet
items.text: Report cards come home, college and career talk starts, and they go quiet. In PATH 101 they choose a goal for school or beyond and work out the next step themselves.

image.alt: Two young students sit on a bench in a school hallway writing in their notebooks

items.label: College and young adults
items.title: A semester in, or a year out
items.text: A first semester that didn't go to plan, or a job that isn't going anywhere. Most people your age are still figuring it out. Here you get one goal down on paper and the steps toward it.

image.alt: Young adults and an older man read and take notes at a long library table

items.label: Parents
items.title: Another adult in their corner
items.text: You want someone besides you that your teen will talk to about what comes next. Parents are welcome on Tuesday mornings too.

image.alt: A father sits beside his teenage son on a bed and talks with him

options.footnote: PATH 101 works on goals and next steps. It doesn't promise grades, college admission or a job.
options.cta: Ask if it fits my family

story.title: About Benny
paragraphs: Benny Carson Sr. was born and raised in Portland, Oregon. He started young, working beside his father in the family business. After high school he spent more than 25 years in corporate retail, in marketing, management, and employee performance and growth.

Along the way he held leadership roles in community groups including Rotary Club, the YMCA and Junior Achievement, served on nonprofit boards and committees, and coached and mentored young people. Today he runs ACHIEVE Mentorship.
In his words: "My desire is to always be engaged in positive growth and the well-being of our youth and families, schools and community."

sponsorship.title: Ask whether a sponsorship could fit your family
sponsorship.text: Ask on your free call, once you've talked about the goal itself. That goes for parents of a teen, for young adults booking their own call, and for parents with a goal of their own. If you're a good fit, you may qualify for a NowTRANSFORMED sponsorship toward this offer.

steps.title: Tell us who you are
steps.text: Your first name, email and age, then pick a time up to three weeks out.

steps.title: Free 15-minute call
steps.text: The NowTRANSFORMED team asks what the young person would like help with, explains how the workshop works and looks at whether you may qualify for a sponsorship. A parent joins for anyone under 18.

steps.title: Decide together
steps.text: Talk it over at home. If it fits, the next step is a Tuesday morning.

faqs.a: You'll get the price of PATH 101, and what it covers, on your free call. Ask about a NowTRANSFORMED sponsorship then too.

faqs.q: When and where does it meet?
faqs.a: Tuesdays, 7:00 to 7:30 a.m. Pacific time, on Zoom. Ask on your free call how many weeks it runs and when you can start.

faqs.q: 7 a.m.? My son won't be up that early.
faqs.a: Maybe not. Let him sit in on the free call and decide for himself.

faqs.q: She already has a school counselor.
faqs.a: Good. This adds to that. Here the goal is hers, in her own words.
It's 15 minutes with the NowTRANSFORMED team. They ask what the young person would like help with, explain how the workshop works and answer your questions. There's nothing to prepare.

faqs.q: How are young people looked after?
faqs.a: For anyone under 18, a parent is on the free call with the NowTRANSFORMED team. That's the place to ask how Benny runs the workshop and handles messages with young people, and anything else you want to know.

Library Talks, a Wednesday morning community conversation on leadership, teamwork, service and responsible citizenship, for high schoolers, young adults, parents and others. It isn't fully set up yet. Ask about it on your free call.
ACHIEVE Mentorship is Benny's own. The free call is with the NowTRANSFORMED team. NowTRANSFORMED is a youth leadership development program.

closing.title: One goal. One next step.
closing.text: A free 15-minute call with the NowTRANSFORMED team. Pick a time up to three weeks out.
